submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole reacts to the context read so far: it fires on the token position at which the model's next-token distribution puts appreciable mass on a 'follow' word - English follow/follows/followed/following ('as follows', 'it follows that', 'followed by', 'must follow'), German fol-/folgen ('aus den folgenden', 'wie folgt') and the Dutch stem vol- ('de cursus graag vol[gen]') - peaking on the token immediately before it, with strength rising with that probability (P(follows)=0.97 at 'The rules are as' gives 35, P=0 at 'The baby is as' gives 0, and the follow word itself never fires). What decides it is the prediction at that position, not the printed continuation ('The results are as expected' fires exactly as much as 'The results are as follows'), and the pole's write opposes what it detects: it subtracts the follow family from the candidate set (suppressing follow/跟随/follows, raising expected/shown/is) and adds ' vol'; a few Dutch mid-word peaks ('filmpje', 'vragen') are unexplained.
